about: The stages of the Nuclear Builder (extensions/tools/nuclear-builder/src/engine.ts).

rows.title: Stage 8 of the Builder: Artifacts
rows.summary: The project is built and its output kept with the run (generated code, contract, OpenAPI).
body: The project is built and its output kept with the run (generated code, contract, OpenAPI).
Who takes part: shell. The stage after it: `deploy`.

rows.title: Stage 5 of the Builder: Code
rows.summary: The local coder (qwen2.5-coder:3b) writes each piece with the Smart Graph and repairs it with the compiler; Claude only fixes what it could not.
body: The local coder (qwen2.5-coder:3b) writes each piece with the Smart Graph and repairs it with the compiler; Claude only fixes what it could not. Ends with nuclear check of the whole project, the tests included.
Who takes part: coder, tester, graph, claude, shell. The stage after it: `verify`.

rows.title: Stage 9 of the Builder: Deploy
rows.summary: Seeds, integration tests and the local deploy of .nuclear/builder.json; the same commands the exported CI runs on a server.
body: Seeds, integration tests and the local deploy of .nuclear/builder.json; the same commands the exported CI runs on a server.
Who takes part: shell. It is the last stage.

rows.title: Stage 2 of the Builder: Generate
rows.summary: nuclear gen writes what follows from the data, already compiling: for each resource of the spec (its GET <url> lines, or its Resources) the models, the repository, a use case per action, the facade, the controller or the screen, the tests.
body: nuclear gen writes what follows from the data, already compiling: for each resource of the spec (its GET <url> lines, or its Resources) the models, the repository, a use case per action, the facade, the controller or the screen, the tests. The agents write only what is left.
Who takes part: shell. The stage after it: `plan`.

rows.title: Stage 3 of the Builder: Plan
rows.summary: The work split into pieces of one file each, in the order they can be written.
body: The work split into pieces of one file each, in the order they can be written. Claude plans when it leads; otherwise the local planner (gemma4:e2b) does.
Who takes part: claude, planner, graph. The stage after it: `test`.

rows.title: Stage 7 of the Builder: Security
rows.summary: The local reviewer reads each new file against the platform's security rules; the project's security commands run.
body: The local reviewer reads each new file against the platform's security rules; the project's security commands run.
Who takes part: security, shell. The stage after it: `artifacts`.

rows.title: Stage 1 of the Builder: Specification
rows.summary: The spec you wrote or imported, with its acceptance criteria and the context the agents get, written to specs/<id>/spec.md.
body: The spec you wrote or imported, with its acceptance criteria and the context the agents get, written to specs/<id>/spec.md. Then its analysis: which kind of request it is (a whole system, one screen, a rename, a failing test...) and the strategy the run follows: the stages that run, what the generators write, the facts it lacks.
Who takes part: you, planner. The stage after it: `generate`.

rows.title: Stage 4 of the Builder: Tests first
rows.summary: Before any code, the local tester writes the tests from the acceptance criteria, the planned pieces and the project map (.nuclear/map.md): what the code must do, in Nuclear.
body: Before any code, the local tester writes the tests from the acceptance criteria, the planned pieces and the project map (.nuclear/map.md): what the code must do, in Nuclear.
Who takes part: tester, graph. The stage after it: `code`.

rows.title: Stage 6 of the Builder: Verification
rows.summary: The project is built and every test runs.
body: The project is built and every test runs. A failing test goes back to the coder told in Nuclear (nuclear explain: the message, a hint and the .nuc lines), then the tests run again (at most 3 rounds); Claude takes what is left when it leads.
Who takes part: shell, coder, tester, claude. The stage after it: `security`.
